trait-impl-decl.comment: `trait`/`impl`/`for` are new reserved keywords. This section is included BEFORE `#control-keywords`/`#storage-keywords` in the top-level `patterns` list (rather than also listing `trait`/`impl`/`for` in those bare-keyword sections, the way `struct`/`enum`/`fn` do) so that its longer, more specific matches win the same-start-position tie against a bare keyword-only match -- otherwise the bare match would consume just the keyword and leave the trait/type name(s) that follow unmatched (no compensating rule like `#function-calls` catches a name that's followed by `for`/whitespace rather than `(`/`{`).

patterns.comment: `trait Shape { ... }` -- capture the declared trait name distinctly from an ordinary identifier.

`impl Shape for Rect { ... }` -- trait impl: both the trait name and the implementing type are type references. Listed before the no-`for` form below so it wins the tie for `impl` headers that do have a `for`.
`impl Rect { ... }` -- inherent impl: the implementing type.

builtin-type-name.comment: Shared by `#trait-impl-decl`'s captures: an impl header's type/trait name gets the more specific `support.type.builtin.mah` scope when it's one of the built-in type/trait names, otherwise the ordinary `entity.name.type.mah`.

builtin-types.comment: Built-in type names (`Number`, `String`, `Bool`, `Function`, `Option`, `Promise`) and the built-in `Printable` trait, wherever they appear as a bare identifier outside an impl header (which `#trait-impl-decl` already handles via `#builtin-type-name`).

self-identifiers.comment: `self`/`Self` are ordinary identifiers syntactically (no dedicated grammar rule -- see grammar.js), so they're recognized positionally here by literal text, the same way `#constants` recognizes `none`.

patterns.comment: `struct Point` / `enum Shape` -- capture the declared type name distinctly from an ordinary identifier.
`fn name(...)` -- named function declarations (anonymous `fn(...)` falls through to the plain storage-keyword rule).

await-field.comment: M10 (async): `.await` is a postfix pseudo-field (ordinary field-access grammar, `"await"` special-cased at codegen time -- see docs/V2_DESIGN.md's M10 milestone), not a real keyword token -- highlighted positionally, mirroring how `#function-calls` above recognizes call sites by shape rather than by a dedicated grammar rule.

patterns.comment: A plain identifier immediately followed by `(` -- a call site, or an enum/struct type name immediately followed by `{` -- a literal construction.
patterns.name: entity.name.function.call.mah
